sources.title: Authorization API 1.0
sources.version_status: Final; published 11 January 2026 as stated in the retrieved document.
supports: Subject/action/resource/context authorization exchange already exists.
A successful decision has a required boolean decision and optional context; an application must explicitly map review and processing failures.
limits: Does not standardize an Action-Effect context attribute or prove the truth of mapped effects.
Successful transport or a PDP failure is not automatically a correct semantic denial.
sources.verification_scope: Complete response retrieved; listed relevant source sections inspected.

sources.title: RFC 9396: OAuth 2.0 Rich Authorization Requests
supports: Structured authorization details and separate objects for distinct permission combinations already exist.
Type-specific semantics determine comparison; the RFC does not define a universal arbitrary-details subset comparator.
Requested details, granted details assigned to a token, and resource-server enforcement are distinct.
limits: Tuple preservation is not novel solely because Action-Effect also requires it.
A request or effect description is not a current authority grant.
sources.verification_scope: Complete response retrieved; listed relevant source sections inspected.

additional_inspections.purpose: Separate permission objects and type-specific comparison.

supports: The Data API accepts structured input and returns evaluated documents.

Strict built-in error handling is a declared API option, not something to assume implicitly.
limits: A required total-decision wrapper must validate outputs; HTTP status alone is insufficient.
Documentation alone does not establish the installed engine; current_measured_evidence separately records the actual OPA 1.21.2 report and binary identity.

sources.title: Cedar authorization documentation
sources.version_status: Commit-pinned documentation; no engine release or execution is claimed.
supports: Cedar requests use principal, action, resource and context.
Default deny, forbid-overrides-permit and skip-on-error are explicit semantics, with determining-policy and error diagnostics.
An error in one policy can coexist with an Allow from another policy.
limits: Review and stricter profile failure handling require a declared wrapper rather than invented native semantics.
Cedar is a future comparison seam in this draft, not an executed pilot lane.
